For Elias Thorne, this was not an anomaly but a rhythm, as predictable as the tide’s pull on the granite cliffs of Blackwood Point. He had tended the light for thirty-two years, his life measured in rotations of the Fresnel lens and the rhythmic thud of the oil pump.
